resolutions.researcher_notes: Replaces the dead attaqa.net original. Value 'construction' supported: PressTV (18 Apr 2023) quotes the Iran Gas Engineering & Development Co. CEO that Iran 'had begun laying the pipeline... from Minab to Kuh Mubarak'; Pipeline Technology Journal (6 Apr 2023) states the first 120-km section Minab-Sirik is 'almost 87% complete' and the second section Sirik-Kuhmobarak 'began in February'. Two separate outlets, though both trace to the same April-2023 NIGC (Reza Noshadi) statement. NOTE/flag: active construction is on the ONSHORE Iranian trunk (Minab-Sirik-Kuhmobarak) toward the coast; the offshore undersea leg to Oman itself is not yet under construction. GEM 'construction' is defensible but reflects the domestic segment.

ProposalYear 2003 supported by Iran International (22 May 2022): 'Iran and Oman signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in 2003 to construct a 200-km pipeline from Iran's Kuh-e Mobarak to Oman's Sohar port'. Single strong source (medium). CONTRADICTION to flag: Anadolu Agency (aa.com.tr) states the two countries 'first signed a Memorandum of Understanding in 2013' - a common alternate origin date some sources use (2013 = the $60bn 25-year supply deal). The 2003 date refers to the earlier MoU; kept as-is per iranintl. Could not verify a clean second independent source stating 2003 explicitly.

Replaces the dead Tehran Times 428285 original. SegmentCost 1,200,000,000 USD supported by two independent outlets: Iran International (2003 MoU 'estimated at the time to cost about $1.2 billion') and Egypt Oil & Gas ('the pipeline project, which is estimated to cost around $1.2 billion'). Both state ~$1.2 billion; value confirmed.

Pipeline II = the NEW 125-km line + 3 compressor stations that Iranian companies agreed on 3 July 2024 (Ashgabat) to build to raise Turkmen gas deliveries to Iran along the Dovletabad-Serakhs-Khangeran route. As of the announcement it is to-be-built / future construction, i.e. 'proposed' — consistent with the sheet value. Widely reported by independent outlets (News Central Asia regional desk, RFE/RL, World-Energy); replaces the dead mfa.gov.tm/news/4626 seed. All three verified 200 + content present.

Both sources describe it explicitly as a natural-gas pipeline supplying gas from Turkmenistan to Iran (and onward swap to Iraq). Fuel = Gas fully supported. Two independent outlets. Replaces dead neftegaz.ru seed.

No source uses the literal word 'transmission' (contains_value=false). PipelineType=transmission is a GEM schema classification, and it is consistent with the described asset: a long-distance (125-km) cross-border gas trunk line moving bulk export volumes, not a distribution/gathering line. Sources support the physical description that underpins the classification; verify the schema tag rather than expecting the word verbatim. [QC] no verified corroborating ref -> dead_link.

CONTRADICTION/DERIVED VALUE FLAG: no source states 19.5 bcm/y directly (contains_value=false). The sheet's 19.50 bcm/y is a GEM derivation: planned total deliveries to Iran = 40 bcm/y, minus existing Pipeline I (12.5 bcm/y) and Korpeje-Kordkuy via Chalyouk metering station (8 bcm/y) = 40 - 20.5 = 19.5 bcm/y as the incremental Pipeline II capacity. nCa source verified to contain the 12.5, 8 and 40 figures; World-Energy contains the 40. Note the 12.5/8/40 numbers all trace to the single 3 July 2024 Turkmen MFA press release (so independent=false), and no source attributes 19.5 to this new line specifically — flag for human review whether 19.5 should stand as computed. [QC] no verified corroborating ref -> dead_link.

Both sources name the supply corridor 'Dovletabad - Serakhs - Khangeran' (= Dauletabad-Sarakhs-Khangiran). nCa verified to contain both 'Dovletabad' and 'Khangeran'. Supports StartLocation=Dauletabad (Ahal Province, Turkmenistan) and EndLocation=Khangiran (Razavi Khorasan Province, Iran); the new 125-km line and compressor stations sit on the Turkmen side feeding this route. Endpoint city/route names corroborated by two independent outlets. Fills the previously-blank Location [ref].

No source supports ProposalYear=2022. Evidence contradicts it: Shana/Petroenergy (en.shana.ir/news/227033, Oct 2014) reports IGAT-11 design was already COMPLETE in 2014; mizenaft.ir/news/27490 states the plan was initiated in 1390 (=2011) under Javad Owji's NIGC tenure. GlobalData's '2022' refers to an assumed CONSTRUCTION start, not the proposal. So the project was proposed ~2011 and designed by 2014, roughly a decade before 2022. ProposalYear should likely be 2011 (or 2014). CONTRADICTION FLAGGED. Left UNRESOLVED rather than cite a source for a value it disproves.

GlobalData headlines IGAT XI as the longest planned Middle East pipeline 'by 2026', supporting StartYear1=2026. CONFLICT: the same GlobalData analysis (as reprinted by worldpipelines.com/project-news/10012022/) states operation 'expected to start ... in 2025', and the underlying date is a GlobalData assumption, not an operator commitment. Single-origin (GlobalData; worldpipelines/pipeline-journal are reprints). Flagged 2025-vs-2026 discrepancy.

Capacity 110 MMSCMD corroborated by two independent Iranian sources plus GlobalData: Shana/Petroenergy (Oct 2014) '110 mcm/d of gas'; mizenaft.ir '110 میلیون متر مکعب گاز در روز'. GlobalData/worldpipelines independently state 110,000 mmcm/d. Consistent across all origins.

Length 1200 km corroborated by Shana/Petroenergy 2014 ('1200 kilometers') independently of GlobalData (worldpipelines reprint: '1200 km'). Minor discrepancy: mizenaft.ir cites the ORIGINAL design at ~1100 km with a proposed +~400 km rerouting, so length has varied with route changes; 1200 km is well supported for the current spec.
Diameter 56 in corroborated by Shana/Petroenergy 2014 ('56-inches') independently of GlobalData (worldpipelines: 'maximum diameter of 56 in.'). Consistent.

START = Asaluyeh, Bushehr: strongly corroborated (Shana 2014, mizenaft.ir, and GlobalData/worldpipelines all cite Asalouyeh origin). END = Bazargan, West Azerbaijan: single-origin (GlobalData via worldpipelines: 'from Asalouyeh ... through Ahvaz, Dehgolan, to the Bazargan'). CONTRADICTION FLAGGED: Shana's original 2014 design routed IGAT-11 through Bushehr/Fars/Yazd/Esfahan/Semnan to tie into the Tehran-Mashhad line (NOT to Bazargan), and mizenaft describes a later route change branching off IGAT-7. The Bazargan (NW border) terminus reflects the newer routing and rests on GlobalData alone; start is high-confidence, end is medium.

Cost USD 4 billion supported only by GlobalData ('estimated to cost 4 billion dollars'), reprinted by worldpipelines/pipeline-journal — one origin. No independent Iranian corroboration of the $4bn total found; mizenaft.ir only cites an incremental ~$2bn cost from the ~400 km reroute plus €1–1.8bn for extra compressors, which is a different figure. Single-origin, medium confidence.

Value 'construction' is supported: in Feb 2024 Pakistan's caretaker cabinet approved the first phase (80 km border-to-Gwadar section), formally moving the project into the construction phase; Iran's ~900 km section is already built. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: multiple sources (The Diplomat Jan 2025; the current-ref Reuters headline 'remains stalled') note that physical construction on the Pakistani side had NOT actually broken ground as of 2024-2025 despite the approval, so 'construction' reflects the approved/nominal phase rather than active groundwork. Replaced the DEAD_LINK Reuters ref (401 bot-wall, and Wayback also 401) with four working independent outlets (World Pipelines, The Nation PK, Outlook India, The Diplomat).

StartYear1=2024 is supported as the year Pakistan approved and committed to start construction of its section (Feb 2024, 80 km border-to-Gwadar first phase). All three sources are Feb 2024 and carry the 2024 date + start-of-construction framing. Note: Iran's section construction dates to ~2011 and full commissioning remains pending, so 2024 specifically marks the Pakistani-side (re)start rather than commissioning.

FuelSource='South Pars gas field' confirmed by two independent sources: Offshore Technology (GlobalData project profile) states the pipeline 'will carry gas from the South Pars field', and GlobalSecurity.org independently names South Pars as the source field. Consistent with all coverage: gas is processed at Asaluyeh, the South Pars onshore terminal.

Route endpoints and provinces corroborated by 2+ independent sources. Iranian start: ISSI (Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad, verified via pdftotext since the verifier cannot substring-match this PDF) names Bushehr; Offshore Technology places the start at the 'Pars energy economic zone' (= Asaluyeh, the South Pars onshore terminal town, which lies in Bushehr province) — so StartLocation=Asaluyeh / StartState=Bushehr / Iran is supported. Pakistani end: ISSI, Offshore Technology, and GlobalSecurity all name Nawabshah, and ISSI + Offshore Technology name Sindh — supports EndLocation=Nawabshah / EndState=Sindh / Pakistan. Minor wording note: the exact token 'Asaluyeh' does not appear verbatim on the verified independent pages (they say 'Pars energy economic zone'/'Bushehr'), but the identification is unambiguous.

SegmentCost=$7,500,000,000 USD supported by three independent sources each carrying the '$7.5 billion' figure (Offshore Technology/GlobalData, Iran International, Outlook India). This is the widely cited total project cost; SegmentCostUnits=USD confirmed. Note the figure is the whole-project estimate (not a segment-specific cost) and long predates recent phase-cost estimates (e.g. ~$158M for the 80 km Gwadar first phase).

Both sources describe a Feb-2019 inter-corporate agreement/MoU only for a feasibility study, carried out by Gazprom at its own expense before any construction decision. Supports 'proposed' status. NOTE: never advanced beyond feasibility; no independent recent (post-2019) evidence found, consistent with the STALE->shelved verdict. Old warsawinstitute.org ref (current Status ref) still resolves 200 but the dead Reuters link is superseded by these two.
Agreement signed early Feb 2019 (thenews: Feb 7, 2019; geo.tv: Feb 6, 2019). Supports ProposalYear 2019. Replaces the dead Reuters ref.

Both sources give a range of 500 MMcf/d to 1 billion cf/d. The recorded Capacity 1000 MMcf/d = 1 bcf/d is the UPPER bound of that quoted range (not a point figure). Value supported but note the range.

Both sources state the project cost as $10 billion USD. Supports SegmentCost 10,000,000,000 USD. Warsaw Institute verified to contain '10 billion'; thenews headline/body cite '$10 bn'. This is a feasibility-study estimate, not a contracted figure.

Shana (official NIOC news, 2024) describes IGAT-9 sections still 'under construction' (Bidboland-Ahvaz section still under construction). World Pipelines (2020) lists it as an upcoming/under-construction trunkline with a projected 2022 start. Two independent outlets support 'construction'. Supersedes the two dead current_refs (iclg / energypress).

World Pipelines (Jan 2020) explicitly gives IGAT-9 an expected start of 2022 (matches StartYear1=2022). Note: this was a projection; per Shana the line was still under construction into 2024/2025, so the 2022 start was not achieved. Single strong source for the projected year -> medium.

Offshore Energy states IGAT-9 adds 110 million cubic meters/day. 110 MMcm/d = ~3,885 MMcf/d (x35.31), which matches Capacity=3885.00 MMcf/d exactly. 110 mcm/d is the widely reported design capacity; only offshore-energy verified as raw text (Financial Tribune capacity article is JS-rendered, nrgedge 403), so medium.

CONTRADICTION: GEM LengthKnown=1,900 km is higher than every located source. Offshore Energy and Shana both give 1,800 km; World Pipelines gives 1,863 km. contains_value=false because none state 1,900. Recommend GEM review length toward ~1,800-1,873 km. Refs added document the length range. [QC] no verified corroborating ref -> unresolved.
Both Shana (56-inch mainline) and Offshore Energy (56-inch project) confirm the 56 in mainline diameter; matches Diameter=56. Two independent outlets -> high. Supersedes dead ghods-niroo current_ref.

Both Shana articles state the line carries South Pars gas from the Assaluyeh onshore refineries (matches FuelSource='South Pars gas field'). Corroborated in substance by Offshore Energy (Assaluyeh origin = South Pars processing hub). Both explicit refs are Shana (same outlet), so independent=false -> medium.

Shana confirms both endpoints: Assaluyeh origin and Bazargan border crossing in West Azarbaijan Province (matches StartLocation=Asaluyeh, EndLocation=Bazargan, EndState=West Azerbaijan). Offshore Energy independently confirms Assaluyeh origin routed through western provinces to Turkey's border. Two independent -> high.

CONTRADICTION: GEM SegmentCost=8,900,000,000 USD (2014). Two independent 2014 sources (Shana and Offshore Energy) both put NIGC's planned investment at 8.5 billion USD, not 8.9 billion. contains_value=false (no source states 8.9B). Recommend GEM correct to 8.5 billion USD (2014). Refs added document the cost. [QC] no verified corroborating ref -> dead_link.

STATUS CONTRADICTS GEM VALUE 'construction' -> supports the CHANGE to 'operating'. Mehr News (16 Mehr 1404 / 2025-10-07), citing Iran Gas Engineering & Development Co CEO, reports the 20-inch Behbahan–Gachsaran line 'joined the gas network' (به شبکه گاز پیوست) with successful gas-injection operations begun. Shana (oil-ministry agency, ~Feb 2026) lists it among ~800 km of trunklines commissioned in year 1404: 'خط لوله بهبهان - گچساران نیز به طول ۶۱ کیلومتر به شبکه گاز پیوسته است'. Two independent operating statements -> recommend Status = operating (StartYear ~2025).

Both name a gas (گاز / 'Gas') pipeline. Iran Ertebat (contractor page, archived): '20″ Gas pipeline construction project between Behbahan/Gachsaran'. Mehr: 'to شبکه گاز' (gas network) with gas injection. Fuel = Gas well corroborated.

'transmission' not stated verbatim, but Mehr describes a 61 km 20-inch trunkline built by Iran Gas Engineering & Development Co with one launcher station, one receiver station, two intermediate valve stations, feeding CGS stations, a petrochemical plant, cement factory and power plant via 4-16 inch off-take branches -- an unambiguous gas transmission (خط انتقال) line, not distribution. PipelineType = transmission supported structurally; single source, hence medium.

Iran Ertebat (contractor) archived page states 'Contract Date: 2022' and the page was published 2022-12-04, consistent with ProposalYear = 2022. Single source; contract award rather than an explicit proposal date, so medium.

No source states StartYear1 = 2024. Timeline found: contract Dec 2022 with a 15-month period (Iran Ertebat), and commissioning / gas injection Oct 2025 (Mehr). A 2024 construction-start is plausible mid-build but not directly attested by any source; leaving UNRESOLVED. If a start date is wanted, the in-service year is 2025 (Mehr, 16 Mehr 1404).

Iran Ertebat supports 62 km ('approximate length of 62 kilometers'). LENGTH DISCREPANCY to flag: the later official/commissioning sources give 61 km for the built mainline -- Mehr (2025-10-07): '61 کیلومتر خط لوله ۲۰ اینچ'; Shana: 'به طول ۶۱ کیلومتر'. GEM 62.00 is the pre-build 'approximate' figure; recommend LengthKnown = 61 km (plus ~10 km of branches) per the as-built sources.
Two independent sources: Iran Ertebat '20″ Gas pipeline' and Mehr 'خط لوله ۲۰ اینچ' (20-inch). Diameter = 20 in well corroborated (mainline; off-take branches are 4-16 in).

The line runs Behbahan -> Gachsaran and is fed from the Behbahan end, where it ties into the national grid (gas injected from that side per Mehr). FuelSource = Behbahan consistent with the origin/feed point. Single explicit source, medium.

Both name the endpoints Behbahan (start) and Gachsaran (end). Behbahan is a city in Khuzestan province (StartState/Province = Khuzestan, established); Gachsaran lies in Kohgiluyeh & Boyer-Ahmad -- Iran Ertebat lists project 'Location: kohgiluyeh', i.e. the end/destination province. Endpoints and Iran country well corroborated; StartState Khuzestan not stated verbatim in these sources but is Behbahan's province.

Owner1 'Iran Ministry of Petroleum' 100% supported by Egypt Oil & Gas: 'The ministry of petroleum is responsible for carrying out this project that has to be implemented through two undersea and land phases' (quoting NIGC CEO / Deputy Petroleum Minister Hamidreza Araqi). Single strong source (medium). Consistency note: offshore-technology.com profile attributes ownership to 'National Iranian Oil and others' with operation by NIGEC/NIGC - NIGC/NIOC are state entities under the Ministry of Petroleum, so the Ministry-level 100% attribution is consistent, not conflicting.

Owner1=Iran Ministry of Petroleum 100% is a parent-level attribution: sources name the state operator, not the Ministry directly. worldpipelines/GlobalData: operator = National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC); Shana 2014: executed by Iranian Gas Engineering and Development Company (GEDC). Both NIGC and GEDC are wholly state-owned subsidiaries under Iran's Ministry of Petroleum, so 100% Ministry ownership is consistent, but the sources attribute the project to the subsidiary companies rather than naming the Ministry itself.

Owner1='Iran Ministry of Petroleum' 100% is only partially supported. ISSI (verified via pdftotext) and other coverage attribute the Iranian section to the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC), which is a wholly state-owned subsidiary under Iran's Ministry of Petroleum — so ministry ownership of the Iranian portion is reasonable. TWO CONTRADICTIONS TO FLAG: (1) sources name NIGC specifically, not the 'Ministry of Petroleum' by name; (2) the '100%' ignores that the Pakistani portion (border-to-Nawabshah) is owned/built by Pakistan's Inter State Gas Systems (ISGS) - so a cross-border Owner attribution of 100% to a single Iranian entity is questionable and likely should be split Iran(NIGC/Ministry) + Pakistan(ISGS). Marked medium/single-source; recommend Update review of the owner split rather than treating this as green.

Gazprom (Gazprom International) is named as the implementing/lead party and would fund the feasibility study; supports Owner1 = Gazprom. HOWEVER both sources pair Gazprom with Pakistan's state Inter-State Gas Systems Ltd (ISGS/ISGSL) as domestic partner, so Owner1 = Gazprom PJSC 100% is a simplification of a bilateral arrangement, not a confirmed 100% equity stake. Tier lowered to medium for the 100% figure.

World Pipelines states National Iranian Gas Co. owns a 100% equity stake and is the operator; Shana names NIGC as owner/developer. NIGC is wholly state-owned under the Ministry of Petroleum, so GEM's Owner1='Iran Ministry of Petroleum' (100%) is the parent entity -- consistent. Attribution note: direct owner reported as NIGC; reviewer may prefer NIGC over the parent ministry.

Both sources name the project client/developer as Iran Gas Engineering & Development Company (Iran Ertebat: 'Client: Iranian Gas Engineering and Development Company'; Mehr: 'شرکت مهندسی و توسعه گاز ایران', IGEDC). IGEDC is a subsidiary of the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC), itself under NIOC -- consistent with 100% Iranian state ownership. FLAG: the more precise owner/operator is NIGC (via IGEDC), not 'National Iranian Oil Co'; consider Owner1 = National Iranian Gas Co.
